solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Few gathering in order to express disapproval

indicators.note: put in order means the letters of the words few and gathering are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small number of people come together for some purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' reads as one phrase of purpose; split it, 'in order' is the anagram signal and 'to' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagging a raised forefinger is the gesture of scolding someone, so the idiom means to show reproof.

clue.text: From Glasgow, a terrible drink

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the run of words that follows, straddling them

explanation.surface: A dreadful beverage served up by someone from Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' reads as origin, but it signals letters lifted out of 'Glasgow, a terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the plainest liquid one can take, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Device used by poor mimic in Greek on vacation

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are set inside the two outer letters
a word on vacation is emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters of Greek
a poor version of the word mimic is a garbled one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy impersonator in Greece relies on some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Greek to its outer letters; 'poor' scrambles mimic, and 'in' sets the result between them. 'used by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimmick is a trick or contrivance used to attract attention, a kind of device.

clue.text: Gives fish as a friendly gesture

parts.note: hands, as a verb, means passes over or gives
the hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone presents a gift of fish as a token of goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking hands is a customary greeting or sign of agreement between people.

clue.text: See 1
Find big room oddly abandoned in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of each word are dropped, leaving the even ones from find, big and room

explanation.surface: Someone searches out a large hall with odd things left behind in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Work word by word: 'oddly abandoned' keeps letters 2, 4... of each, giving ID, I and OM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set expression whose sense differs from its words, a characteristic turn of phrase.

clue.text: Leave don somewhere in Hampshire

parts.note: to go is to leave or depart
to sport something is to wear it, to don it

explanation.surface: A university lecturer is told to depart from a southern county town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a university lecturer but is the verb, to put on; GOSPORT is a naval town on the Hampshire coast in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a coastal town on the south coast of England, inside the county of Hampshire.

clue.text: Somehow ignore topless bevy? Not with this!

definitions.text: Somehow ignore topless bevy? Not with this!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unspecified order, an anagram
a topless word loses its top, the first letter of bevy

explanation.surface: A man told to look away from a group of bare-chested women would fail if he had a wandering gaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the clue signals an anagram; 'topless' removes the B of bevy, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: with this trait you cannot ignore them.
explanation.definitionFit: A roving eye is a tendency to look at, and flirt with, attractive people other than one's partner.

clue.text: St Augustine's first and main problem is staying power

parts.note: St is the written abbreviation for saint, kept as it is

indicators.note: the first of Augustine's letters only is taken
a problem with the word main means its letters are in trouble, jumbled

explanation.surface: A saint's principal difficulty turns out to be endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' scrambles MAIN into MINA; 'first' takes only the opening letter of Augustine's, while St stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the endurance that lets someone keep going through prolonged effort.

clue.text: Young lady, I have a letter

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
I've is the contracted form of I have

explanation.surface: A girl announces that some post has arrived for her.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a formal or lengthy written message, a letter in the correspondence sense.

clue.text: Masculine nonsense about my bioengineering

indicators.note: tosh goes about, around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: tosh is British slang for nonsense

indicators.note: engineering the letters of my and bio rebuilds them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses another's biotechnology work as macho rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bioengineering' must be split in two: its first three letters are fodder and 'engineering' scrambles them with 'my' into MBOYI; 'about' puts the nonsense word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomboyish describes a girl with boyish, mannish habits, so masculine in manner.

clue.text: Idea for weather-beaten underwear

parts.note: underwear battered by the weather, while the whole word is a sudden idea

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a design for lingerie that withstands rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words the answer pictures a bra caught out in a gale; read as one, it is a flash of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm is a sudden bright notion, or a session generating ideas.

clue.text: Napoleon's declaration?

parts.note: Napoleon is the ruling pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, so his utterance would be a pig's grunt, not the emperor's proclamation

explanation.surface: A historic statement by the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor is the false path; the pig Napoleon in Orwell's Animal Farm only grunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the conventional word for the noise a pig makes.

clue.text: Carry out a pneumonectomy and relax

definitions.meaning: a pneumonectomy removes a lung, so it literally takes away an organ of breathing
to pause for a short rest

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes a lung and then unwinds.
explanation.walkthrough: A breather is literally a lung here, the thing a pneumonectomy takes out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stopping work briefly to rest; the surgical reading treats the lung as a breather.

clue.text: Prime minister individually follows most of Chinese religion

indicators.note: the second piece follows, comes after, the first
most of the word means all but its final letter

parts.note: Taoism is the Chinese religion and philosophy of the Tao
each means individually, one by one

explanation.surface: A national leader adopts, one person at a time, a largely Chinese faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of Taoism, and 'follows' puts the second piece after it. The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoiseach is the Irish title for the head of government, equivalent to a premier.

clue.text: See 13
European banks bar meeting

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its edges, the outer letters of European

parts.note: a counter is the bar over which drinks or goods are served

explanation.surface: Continental banks forbid a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the financial noun but means the edges of European, giving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, especially an unplanned one.

clue.text: Subject to contract initially, you're trained to show politeness

indicators.note: trained letters are drilled into a new formation, rearranged
initially takes the first letter of each of subject, to and contract

explanation.surface: A lawyer advises that, pending contract, being well schooled means being courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives STC, the familiar shorthand for subject to contract; 'trained' mixes it with YOU'RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is polite, considerate behaviour towards others.

clue.text: Platform for remarkable sort in spirit

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

indicators.note: remarkable here suggests the letters of sort are remarkably altered, an anagram

explanation.surface: A stage for an extraordinary character who is full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' scrambles SORT into OSTR, set 'in' RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a kind of dais.

clue.text: Where you might keep money, say

indicators.note: say signals that the answer is pronounced like the word for money

parts.note: cash is money in notes and coins

explanation.surface: A question about where to store money, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' suggests 'for example' but tells you the answer sounds like CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store of goods or valuables, a place to stash things.

clue.text: My face is agreeable

parts.note: my! and cor! are both exclamations of surprise; cor is British slang
dial is slang for face, and also the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Someone claims their own looks are pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, like British 'Cor!', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly in manner, pleasantly amiable.

clue.text: Pass out seeing these scary creatures

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of order, so pass is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone faints at the sight of frightening animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting; 'out' is the anagram signal on PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, the sort of creature many find frightening.

clue.text: Mae 2 perhaps in disguise

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible alternative arrangement of the letters

parts.note: read as a superscript, 2 means squared

explanation.surface: A sequel film starring Mae, maybe with the actor in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mae 2' as Mae squared; 'perhaps' scrambles MAE SQUARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a false show or pretence, a disguise of one's real self.

clue.text: Colour that needs treating before it can become argumentative

indicators.note: the answer joined with the letters of treating can become argumentative when the whole lot is rearranged

explanation.surface: A shade that must be worked on before it turns quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the answer's letters to TREATING and 'can become' rearranges the pool into ARGUMENTATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauve is a pale purple shade, so it names a colour.

clue.text: Was a resident that's out of the world in Berlin

indicators.note: out of shows the second piece is taken out of the first

parts.note: die Welt is German for the world, as said in Berlin
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone lived in Berlin, but in a way detached from reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the world' sounds like 'otherworldly'; in fact IE is removed 'out of' DIE WELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, meaning lived somewhere as an inhabitant.

clue.text: Bob may be storing dry fabric finally in shed

indicators.note: the hut is storing, holding within it, the other pieces

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
to air laundry is to dry it

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of fabric

explanation.surface: A man named Bob might keep drying cloth in his outhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' is a short hairstyle, not a man's name; HUT is 'storing' AIR plus C, which 'finally' takes from fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short, straight hairstyle, so it is one example of a haircut.

clue.text: One not currently working as a footballer

definitions.meaning: a worker who has walked out on strike
the forward whose job is to score goals

explanation.surface: An out-of-work person becomes a soccer player.
explanation.definitionFit: Striker means both a worker in an industrial stoppage and an attacking forward in soccer.

clue.text: Hold up basket

definitions.meaning: a large wicker basket with a lid, as for picnics

explanation.definitionFit: Hamper as a verb means to impede progress, and as a noun a lidded wicker container for food.

clue.text: Weapon permit to get a jewellery item

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: A firearms licence is needed for a piece of ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band or bracelet worn round the upper arm as an ornament.
